notable_anecdotes.description: Dr. Bernal's diagnosis: 'metabolic syndrome with microvascular complication' -- CJ's body could not completely metabolize and absorb nutrients, causing diminished mental and physical capacity; explicitly NOT Alzheimer's. The proposed therapy was tailor-made to this diagnosis using four cell types (MSC, EPC, osteoblasts, chondroblasts) extracted from bone marrow under local anesthesia, processed and expanded in lab, infused intravenously monthly for six months, with some cells frozen for future use.

one_paragraph_summary: Part 1 of the four-part stem-cell series opens with CJ Panganiban's caveat that he is 'just a simple lawyer who has read many books, interviewed personally and lengthily many doctors... and had undergone personally the two general types of stem cell therapies.' The two types: autologous stem cell (ASC) therapy -- extracting one's own cells (from bone marrow, blood, skin, or other parts), strengthening them in a laboratory, and infusing them back intravenously once a month for six consecutive months -- and living cell therapy (LCT) -- injecting emulsified embryo parts from cancer-resistant black sheep into the patient's buttocks in 10 same-day injections (German law prohibits exporting sheep stem cells). CJ then narrates how he came to ASC under Filipino American Dr. Samuel D. Bernal (MD, PhD, JD, MBA from American universities, clinics in Woodland Hills California and Prague), whose 'miraculous healings' included former Labor Secretary Nieves Confessor's fourth-stage cancer -- still in remission when CJ encountered her at the Feb. 29, 2024 AIM Chapel dedication for his late wife Leni. Three social encounters built rapport before treatment: a June 19, 2012 Archie concert at the Mind Museum, a Feb. 28, 2013 breakfast at Bernal's brother-in-law Ted Laguatan's, and a June 18, 2013 Archie concert at the Carlos P. Romulo auditorium at the RCBC. Asked about his 'diminishing physical and mental agility,' Bernal requested CJ's seven thick medical albums chronicling his condition since 1983; on July 15, 2013, Bernal and Dr. Denise Labilles handed CJ a five-page comprehensive summary and diagnosed 'metabolic syndrome with microvascular complication' -- capillaries failing to deliver blood, inadequate nutrient absorption -- explicitly not Alzheimer's. CJ agreed 'right then and there, without consulting my wife Leni' to bone-marrow extraction under local anesthesia, with four cell types (mesenchymal, endothelial progenitor, osteoblasts, chondroblasts) to be cultured for six monthly intravenous infusions, with some cells frozen for future use. Fees were P2,222,544 full / P1,778,035 with 20% senior discount, split P480,000 to Medical City and P1,298,035 to Globetek Science Foundation, with up to P5 million for difficult cancer cases; Dr. Labilles waived her own professional fees. Medical City president-CEO Dr. Alran Bengzon (a neurologist) had conducted due diligence on Bernal -- all 'A-1' -- but what 'truly convinced him' was Bernal's own healing of Bengzon's stomach cancer after American doctors gave up. CJ went home five hours after the consultation, the bone-marrow extraction, and the Bengzon conversation.
